text: Do not pay any fee, deposit or kit charge before a signed offer from a verified employer. Genuine employers do not charge applicants to apply, interview or join.
Never share an OTP, card PIN, CVV or UPI PIN with a recruiter. No hiring process needs them.
Do not send Aadhaar, PAN, passport or bank details before you have verified the employer and received a written offer. Ask why each document is needed and when.
Compare the stated pay with similar roles on several job boards. Pay far above the usual range for the role is a reason to verify more carefully.
Treat any guarantee of a job or placement as a reason to ask for details in writing. Ask what selection steps apply and who makes the final decision.
Ask for the company's registered legal name and look it up in the MCA company search (mca.gov.in). Check that the address and directors are consistent with the listing.
Look up when the company website domain was registered using a public WHOIS lookup. A very recent domain for a company claiming a long history needs an explanation.
Ask the recruiter to write from an email address on the company's own website domain, then confirm that address on the company's official contact page.
Compare the domain in the recruiter's email with the domain of the company website. If they differ, ask for an explanation and check the spelling for look-alike domains.
Move the conversation to an official channel (company email or the careers page) instead of chat apps. Be cautious with offers that only use WhatsApp or Telegram.
Ask for a live interview over video, phone or in person with a named interviewer. Be cautious if hiring is decided only through chat or without any interview.
Take your time. A genuine employer will allow you to read the offer and ask questions. Pressure to decide today is a reason to pause and verify.
Ask for the full job description, reporting manager, team, work location and working hours in writing. Vague answers are worth noting.
Check that the required skills and responsibilities are specific and match the role title. Ask how your work will be assessed.
Some wording in this listing resembles wording often seen in risky listings. This is a pattern, not proof. Verify the employer independently before sharing anything.
The contact email matches the company website, which is a positive signal but not proof. Still confirm the recruiter on the company's official page before sharing documents.
A structured interview is a positive signal. Still confirm the interviewer's name and role on the company's official page.
Find the recruiter on the company's official page or professional profile and message them there to confirm the opportunity is genuine.
Read the offer letter and any contract fully before signing. Check the stated pay, notice period, bond or penalty terms and the company's legal name and address.
If any payment is ever requested, stop and verify first. Use traceable methods only after verification, keep receipts, and never pay through personal accounts or gift cards.
Share the offer with a trusted person, a mentor or your college placement cell and ask them to review it before you accept.
If you have already lost money, call the national cybercrime helpline 1930 and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in as soon as possible, and tell your bank.
Keep screenshots of messages, emails, payment requests and the listing in case you need to report it to the platform or the authorities.
